title: Signal enrichment & routing playbook for console reporting requests
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers continually submit console and reporting asks (usage exports, cost breakdowns, scheduled dashboards, ad-hoc queries) via multiple channels (support, customer success, growth, in-console request widget). We lack a repeatable, data-driven triage process that: 1) enriches incoming signals, 2) routes requests to the right delivery lane (self-serve, quick export, engineering backlog, premium build), and 3) provides transparent ETA and prioritization rationale to customers and internal stakeholders.

Goals: Define an operational playbook and a light-weight signal enrichment pipeline that can be implemented by Console and Growth teams to reduce manual triage time, increase delivery predictability, and ensure high-value enterprise asks are surfaced to product engineering with sufficient context. The playbook should produce a prioritized queue with suggested routing, an automated SLA estimate, and an audit trail for compliance-sensitive customers.

Scope: This ticket covers the product-side spec and prioritization rules for the enrichment + routing pipeline, plus sample UI copy for the in-console request form and the PM/Eng intake dashboard. Implementation (data pipeline + classifier + queue automation) will be tracked in follow-up engineering tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical request schema: sample request fields defined (tenant tier, revenue band, sample query/payload, export frequency, retention requirements, PII flag, urgency) and validated with support and CS teams.

Signal enrichment matrix: mapping of raw inputs to enriched features (similar existing ask detection via embeddings, estimated customer value, estimated engineering cost, compliance flag) documented and approved.

Routing lanes defined with acceptance gates: Self-serve (auto-approved), Quick Export (SLA 3 business days), Analytics Backlog (prioritized engineering work), Enterprise Feature (PM approval + roadmap cadence).

Priority scoring formula produced with adjustable weights (customer value, number of affected workspaces, revenue, legal/compliance risk, operational complexity) and example scorecards for 10 recent tickets.
Mockups for in-console request flow and internal intake board created and reviewed by Design and Growth.
Stakeholder sign-off: Support, Customer Success, Growth, Security, and Eng leads have provided explicit feedback or approval in comments.
Transition plan: next steps and at least two ENG tickets created for classifier prototype and intake dashboard integration.
Documentation: short playbook (one-pager) that CS and Support can follow for 90-day pilot attached as link.
decision_record: Use a hybrid approach: start with deterministic rule-based enrichment (tier, export size, PII) and fallback to an ML similarity classifier for duplicate detection; avoids initial ML ops burden and allows rapid shipping.
Prioritization will be customer-value-first with explicit negative weight for compliance risk to surface work requiring legal/secure handling.
Expose score components (why this request has priority X) in the internal intake UI for transparency and auditability rather than a single opaque number.
Keep SLA bands conservative for pilot: Quick Export = 3 business days, Self-serve = immediate, Engineering Backlog = sprint-level ETA provided within one sprint.
implementation_notes: Proposed enriched features: tenant_tier, annual_spend_band, request_type (export|dashboard|alert|dashboard-edit), estimated_row_count, contains_pii (y/n), similarity_to_existing (embedding cosine), historical_duplicate_count, requested_by_role.

Suggested data sources: billing records (for spend band), recent support tickets (for duplicates), workspace metadata (for feature usage), and a tiny embedding index of canonical deliverables (past export templates & dashboards).
Initial classifier: lightweight vector similarity (Cosine > 0.82) + heuristics (contains_pii + >1M rows => enterprise lane). Defer full ML ranking to subsequent cycle.
Privacy: requests flagged contains_pii must trigger encryption-in-transit notes and route to Private/Enterprise lane if tenant policy restricts data extraction.
Engineering follow-ups: ENG-79021 (intake dashboard backend), ENG-79022 (similarity index & embedding pipeline), ENG-79023 (routing automation + queue labels).

notes: Pilot approach: 90-day pilot with top 10 enterprise tenants. Measure: mean triage time reduction, % of asks auto-routed correctly, and stakeholder satisfaction score.
Metrics to track: triage_latency_seconds, percent_auto_routed, average_delivery_lead_time_by_lane, number_of_manual_escalations.
Rollout plan: enable in-console request widget for 10 tenant beta, triage via new intake board; iterate weights monthly based on dev capacity and outcomes.
Fallback & escalation: any request flagged PII + high revenue must go through manual PM review; system should not auto-approve exports that bypass data controls.
